rationale: The issue is that permission_policy is instantiated at module level and its model is cached before test settings overrides take effect. When tests use @override_settings(WAGTAILDOCS_DOCUMENT_MODEL='tests.CustomDocument'), the permission_policy still references the default Document model, causing a model mismatch. The fix ensures get_queryset() uses self.model (which respects settings overrides) to get the base queryset, then intersects it with the permission-filtered queryset. This maintains security (IDOR prevention) while supporting custom document models.
patch:
--- a/wagtail/documents/views/documents.py
+++ b/wagtail/documents/views/documents.py
@@ -222,8 +222,11 @@ class EditView(generic.EditView):
 
     def get_queryset(self):
         # Filter to only documents the user has permission to change
-        return self.permission_policy.instances_user_has_permission_for(
+        # Use self.model to ensure we query the correct model (including custom models)
+        qs = self.model._default_manager.all()
+        permitted_qs = self.permission_policy.instances_user_has_permission_for(
             self.request.user, "change"
         )
+        return qs & permitted_qs
 
     def get_object(self, queryset=None):
